question: to the Commission Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew) Subject:

Negotiations between the EU and the United States on the framework agreement regarding the exchange of personal data, including biometric data, for the purpose of screening and identity verification of travellers1, are expected to be concluded soon. According to the Commission, in this context ‘ensur[ing] respect of the EU’s standards on the protection of personal data’ is a ‘key priority’2. This should not only be the case prior to signing an agreement, but also afterwards, in practice. The EU-US Umbrella Agreement, in force since 2017 and intended to improve the overall level of data protection in EU-US law enforcement cooperation, was supposed to be jointly reviewed by 2020. However, six years later, a joint review report has yet to be published. 1.

Why was no joint review of the EU-US Umbrella Agreement published, despite the legal requirement to do so3? If the data protection requirements of that agreement cannot be reviewed or assessed because there are no results to review, and noting the worrying developments in the US regarding the protection of personal data, how does the Commission expect EU citizens to have trust in the US authorities as regards the safety of their transferred biometric data?

Will the Commission ensure that the draft agreement fully incorporates the standards set by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) in relevant case law4, and if so, is it convinced that the envisaged agreement would hold up in court?
